title: Tenant-aware eviction profiles and evidence orchestration for prompts/responses/logs/metrics
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Problem: Customers need predictable, auditable retention controls that can be expressed per-tenant, per-route, and per-data-class (prompts, responses, request logs, metrics). Existing retention toggles are coarse-grained and do not support sampled retention, conditional legal-hold exceptions, or automated evidence packaging for audits. This causes operational burden for customers in regulated industries and increases legal risk for Redwood.

Proposal: Build a Tenant-aware Eviction Profiles feature + Evidence Orchestration pipeline: (1) retention profiles are first-class objects that can be assigned at tenant, route, or model-route scope; (2) profiles support TTL, sampled retention (percentage or N-in-X), legal-hold tags, and archive-to-S3 exports; (3) evidence orchestration composes signed, time-bound export bundles with provenance metadata for each retention action; (4) admin console + API to author, preview (simulator), and schedule profile changes with dry-run and impact estimates.

Scope (MVP):
- Retention profile model and API for prompts, responses, request_logs, and metrics.
- Per-tenant override precedence and inheritance rules (tenant > route > global).
- Sampled retention engine: rule syntax to keep X% or N items per user/session.
- Evidence exporter: bundle generator (manifest, HMAC-signed index, checksum) for TTL-based and manual exports.
- Console UI: profile editor, applied routes list, retention impact simulator (token/sample counts + storage delta).
- Audit logs & traceability: each eviction/export will record artifact references and LDAT (ISO timestamp), operator, profile id.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Create retention profile resource and CRUD API documented in the API spec.
2) Implement inheritance logic: tenant overrides route overrides global; documented examples.
3) Sampled retention supports percentage and top-N per-session semantics and has unit/integration tests.
4) Evidence exporter produces a signed bundle (manifest.json, artifacts tar.gz, signature.asc) and stores it in configured bucket; export record persisted with export_id.
5) Console UI allows creation/editing of profiles, shows applied routes, and runs a simulator that returns estimated affected token counts and estimated storage delta.
6) Audit trail entries are searchable in Console (last 90 days) and contain profile_id, executor, timestamp, and export_id when applicable.
7) Backwards compatibility: existing tenants without profiles will inherit previous default behavior. Migration plan validated in staging with synthetic traffic.
8) Security review completed and KMS integration verified for signatures.
9) E2E smoke test demonstrating creation->eviction->evidence export with signed manifest and retrieval.
engineering_notes:
Key engineering components:
- Schema: single canonical RetentionProfile object with fields: id, name, scope (global/tenant/route), data_classes (list), ttl_days|ttl_policy (complex), sampling_rule (percent or top_n per key), legal_hold_tags (list), destination_bucket (optional), compress=true/false, export_encryption_kms_key.
- Retention worker: add sampled retention support; integrate with existing purge pipeline (ENG-22456) and deterministic-purge-orchestrator (existing ENG-22456/ENG-33782).
- Evidence orchestration: incremental exporter that can sign manifests with KMS or HSM; use chunked streaming uploads for large artifact bundles.
- Simulator: approximate counts from histogram/service metrics + fast path using time-series TTL distributions.
- Backfill: migration job to tag existing records with effective_profile_id for traceability; must be rate-limited to avoid capacity spikes.
- Observability: retention-run metrics (items_checked, items_deleted, items_exported, export_duration_ms, failed_exports).
- Performance: sampled retention involves sampling decisions at eviction time; ensure batched decisions to avoid N queries per item; leverage existing batching layer in serving runtime where possible.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Storing effective_profile_id on each request row increases storage and write amplification but simplifies audits. Alternative: compute effective profile on export using route history; chosen to favor audit speed (store profile_id).
- Sampling semantics: per-session top-N is heavier than percentage sampling; provide both with opt-in for top-N.
- Evidence bundle format: using tar+manifest+signature for wide compatibility vs. custom protobuf; tar chosen for customer convenience.

Open engineering tasks:
- Define retention_profile schema and migration script (owner: ENG infra).
- Wire KMS signing flow and implement signature verification on download.
- Implement sampling engine and add unit tests with deterministic RNG seeds.
- Add feature flags to enable per-tenant behavior during rollout.
design_notes:
Console UX goals: make retention policies understandable to non-legal users while preserving expressivity for compliance engineers.

Key screens/wires:
- Profiles list: name, scope badge, last run summary, estimated storage delta.
- Editor: scope selector (global/tenant/route), data class toggles, TTL fields with natural language helper ("keep for 90 days"), sampling controls with inline examples, legal-hold toggle with override explanation.
- Simulator modal: allow selecting a time window and sample user IDs; returns a breakdown by data class and example records that would be exported/purged (scrubbed).
- Export history: paginated list with manifest link and verification status.

Accessibility: explainers with in-line help text and a short tutorial for first-time policy creators.

Design attachments: link to mockups (Confluence & Drive) and a color-coded policy precedence diagram for visual clarity.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): implement backend APIs and retention worker; enable for 5 internal tenants behind feature flag; run synthetic traffic for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (pilot): open UI to 10 customers (opt-in) and collect feedback; run live simulator and perform two staged exports to customer test buckets.
Phase 3 (general): enable for all tenants with default profile inherited from previous behavior.
Migration: run backfill tagging in off-peak windows, with throttling and monitoring.
Rollback: disable feature flag and stop worker; keep export bundles in retention for forensics.
Communication: send notice to customers with instructions and opt-out links; update docs and API changelog.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: incorrect deletions causing data loss for customers. Mitigation: add 48-hour soft-delete quarantine for first two production weeks and require manual confirm for non-empty evidence exports.
Risk: performance regression during mass backfill. Mitigation: quota and rate-limit backfill; use small batch sizes and monitor worker lag.
Risk: signatures/keys compromised. Mitigation: rotate signing keys, require KMS audit logs, and include signature verification tool in Console.
Risk: legal_hold complexity across tenants. Mitigation: legal_hold tags are additive and must be honored regardless of profile TTL; block deletions if any active legal_hold exists.
